statements.says: No one may sue without standing and an existing or potential interest recognised by law.
The judge raises of his own motion the plaintiff's or defendant's lack of standing.
The judge also raises of his own motion the lack of a permission where the law requires one.
The action is brought by a written, signed and dated petition lodged at the registry by the plaintiff, his agent or his lawyer, in as many copies as there are parties.
The petition must contain the listed particulars, on pain of inadmissibility in form.
Mandatory element 1: the court before which the action is brought.
Mandatory element 2: the plaintiff's first name, surname and domicile.
Mandatory element 3: the defendant's first name, surname and domicile, or last known domicile if none is known.
Mandatory element 4: for a legal person, its name and nature, registered seat and the capacity of its legal or conventional representative.
Mandatory element 5: a brief statement of the facts, the claims and the grounds on which the action rests.
Mandatory element 6: where appropriate, a reference to the supporting documents.
The petition is registered at once in a special register in order of arrival, with the parties' names, case number and first hearing date.
The registrar notes the case number and first hearing date on the copies and hands them to the plaintiff for formal service on the parties.
At least 20 days must separate delivery of the summons and the first hearing, unless the law says otherwise.
That period is extended to 3 months before all courts if the summoned person lives abroad.
The petition is registered only after payment of the legally fixed fees, unless the law says otherwise.
The court president rules on any dispute over payment of fees by an order not open to any appeal.

A petition concerning a published real property or real right must be published at the land registry and produced at the first hearing at which the case is called, on pain of inadmissibility in form, unless its deposit for publication is proved.
A divorce action by one spouse is brought before the family section by a petition in the forms laid down for bringing an action.
Where the spouse lacks full capacity, the divorce request is made in his name by his guardian or curator.
The divorce plaintiff must formally serve a copy of the petition on the defendant and the public prosecutor.
He may also notify the public prosecutor through the registry.
Conciliation attempts in divorce are mandatory and held in a closed session.
Conciliation attempts in divorce may not exceed 3 months from the filing of the divorce action.

deadlines.startsFromEvent: Delivery of the summons to appear (the period must separate it from the date set for the first hearing)
Delivery of the summons to appear, where the person summoned lives abroad (extends the 20-day period)
Filing of the divorce action (outer limit for conciliation attempts)

priorSteps.requiredWhen: Payment of the legally fixed fees before the petition is registered, in every case.
notRequiredWhen: Where the law provides otherwise (the texts given do not say which cases).
priorSteps.sanctionIfMissing: The petition is not registered (no inadmissibility sanction stated).

priorSteps.requiredWhen: The petition concerns a real property and/or a real right in real property that is published under the law; deposit for publication, and production at the first hearing where the case is called.
priorSteps.sanctionIfMissing: Inadmissibility in form (عدم قبولها شكلا), unless deposit for publication is proved.

priorSteps.requiredWhen: A divorce action before the family section; the attempts are held after filing, within 3 months.

openPoints.question: Does the sanction of inadmissibility in form in article 15 attach to each of the six listed elements, including element 6 (supporting documents) which applies only 'where appropriate'?
readings: Yes: every listed element is under the sanction, and element 6 only when there are documents to cite.
Element 6 is not sanctioned because it is conditional; only elements 1 to 5 are.

openPoints.question: Does a petition missing signature, date, lodging at the registry or the right number of copies (article 14) cost inadmissibility?
readings: No: article 14 states no sanction and these items are not in the article 15 list.
Yes: they are conditions of the written petition, so article 15's sanction reaches them by implication.

openPoints.question: Is article 15 element 4 (legal person: name, nature, seat, representative's capacity) mandatory only when a party is a legal person?
readings: Yes, only for a legal-person party.
It is a general element in all petitions.

openPoints.question: Does the 20-day period in article 16 paragraph 3 run on the summons or on the petition, and how is it counted?
readings: It runs from delivery of the summons to the first hearing date, as written; counting rules are not stated in the texts given.
It is a condition on the whole filing and affects the petition.

openPoints.question: Is the mandatory conciliation attempt in divorce (article 439) a prior step before filing or a step inside the proceedings, and what happens if it is skipped?
readings: It is a step inside the proceedings after filing, within 3 months of filing; no sanction is stated.
It is a precondition to the judge's ruling on the merits.

openPoints.question: Which cases are excused from payment of fees before registration under article 17 paragraph 1, and which publication rules make a right 'published' under article 17 paragraph 3?
readings: The texts given do not say; the fee and land-registry laws are needed.
The petition is exempt where legal aid or a statutory exemption exists (not in the texts given).

openPoints.question: What do 'existing or potential interest' and 'standing' cover in article 13?
readings: Standing is the plaintiff's own personal quality as holder of the right; interest is the benefit sought.
Both are assessed by the judge as the facts show; the texts give no definition.

openPoints.question: The slots on formal notice, non-conciliation records, limitation, forfeiture, administrative grievances, payment orders and the specialised commercial court are not settled by any text given here.
readings: These texts offer no rule to test them for the petition formal elements.

missingTexts.why: Rules on summons, service and the form of the summons referred to in article 16 and article 438.
Provisions on legal capacity and representation of the plaintiff or legal person (needed for standing in articles 13 and 15).
The laws that require a permission (إذن) before suing, referred to in article 13 paragraph 3.
The fees law and any exemption rule referred to in article 17 paragraph 1 ('unless the law says otherwise').
The land-registry and real-property publication rules referred to in article 17 paragraph 3.
Family code provisions referred to in articles 423, 442, 446, 451 on divorce grounds and conditions.
